- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or flat, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model overreacts; cap next-period forecast at +10% above prior true value to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match recent low trend.
- When sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.27→0.44→0.53), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment step.
- If model forecast is >10% above true for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction to prevent overfitting to recent highs.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70.5 for 5+ days, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to capture downward bias.
